messages.content: Analyze this sentence.  "Consydre thou myne condicyon; reflecte upon myne fader. Shall I forsake hym, when he is strycken wyth blyndnesse and destytute, to wrastle wyth infirmitie and penurye, when it lyeth wythin my poure to rendre hys latter yeeres fylled wyth comforte and joye?" Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.

message.content: Analysis of this sentence: the speaker uses archaic diction and a second-person imperative to make the listener weigh the speaker's condition and his father's suffering, then asks a rhetorical question that presents abandoning a blind, destitute, infirm, and poor father as morally monstrous; because he says it is within his power to fill the father's later years with comfort and joy, the passage becomes a forceful appeal to filial duty, mercy, and conscience. Analysis
